A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SiNGER, with matching authors, core methodology, and retained experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable and support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-task distillation results, representation measurements, component analyses, and ablations, including empirical spectral and subspace analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds model configurations, downstream component ablations, Jacobian comparisons, and long-tail entropy measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same low-rank teacher-feature adapter, approximate-nullspace initialization, three losses, and joint optimization procedure. Appendix A's linearization is unchanged. Additional backbones and the Jacobian comparator extend evaluation without establishing a revised SiNGER algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten downstream datasets spanning classification, segmentation, depth, domain shift, and fine-grained recognition. The additions concern model configurations, subsets, and diagnostics within this coverage; the majority/tail analysis further examines the existing iNaturalist2019 task.

E2.justification: FitNet and ViTKD remain the comparators in the original ViT-Large-to-Tiny experiment. The new approximation study introduces a full-Jacobian method as an evaluated comparator for constructing null directions (v3 Table 8).

E3.justification: Tables 1 and 10 expand evaluation from one teacher–student configuration to multiple ViT, DeiT-III, and DINO configurations, including larger and cleaner teachers. New subset-based component and Jacobian tests and majority/tail evaluation introduce additional protocols. Reported ViT-Large/Tiny parameter counts also change from 290.2/5.5M to 304.33/5.72M, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 retains the original alignment, loss, rank, threshold, layer-selection, and visualization analyses. It adds downstream component ablations (Table 4), nonlinear-output preservation against a Jacobian reference (Table 8), cleaner-teacher, cross-family, and scaling analyses (Table 10), long-tail entropy diagnostics (Table 11), and computational-overhead analysis.

E5.justification: The existing per-image mean, standard-deviation, median, and distribution summaries are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new logit-entropy analysis measures predictive confidence rather than statistical uncertainty in the reported performance estimates.

E6.justification: The original ViT-Large-to-Tiny scores remain unchanged, including 70.59 IN-val accuracy, 21.76 mIoU, and 0.9406 depth RMSE. v3 adds substantial results for other configurations and the new diagnostic experiments. Table 1 also changes the iNaturalist comparison from a 2.84-point deficit against non-distilled Tiny to a 1.09-point gain over FitNet, while retaining 41.11 accuracy; this is a changed comparison reference, not improved performance.

T1.justification: The method equations, FFN/SVD construction, approximate-nullspace bound, and principal/null subspace-energy definitions are retained. The new Jacobian comparison supplies empirical evidence, without adding or revising a formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and concluding research claims retain the same meaning: nullspace-guided refinement suppresses artifacts while preserving information and improves distillation and interpretability. Broader experiments add support without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of nonlinear approximation validity, initialization benefits, and potential suppression of useful channels in cleaner teachers. Appendix J replaces the brief citation-based long-tail explanation with a teacher-logit uncertainty account. The explicit limitation that students cannot match SINDER/DINOv3 representation cleanliness is removed. Some added interpretations conflict with results, notably the cleaner-teacher segmentation claims in Appendix C versus Table 10a.

D1.justification: Table 9 adds architectural specifications and GFLOPs. Section 5 reports initialization below 0.2 seconds, approximately 65K adapter parameters, and approximately 10% additional epoch time. The detailed optimizer, hardware, augmentation, and training schedule are retained, as is the promise to release code upon publication.

R1.justification: The long-tail rewrite removes references to Yu et al. (2024) and Huang et al. (2025). Previously cited DINO models receive additional positioning as cleaner-teacher test cases, while the explicit SINDER/DINOv3 cleanliness comparison is removed. The principal related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 adds a Discussion section and architectural/configuration appendices, rewrites the long-tail discussion, and makes localized experimental-description edits. Affiliations, corresponding-author information, and conference headers change. The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and most existing appendix prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially restructured into multiple configuration blocks with separate gain rows and underlined comparators. Five new tables display the added analyses and architecture details; the existing hyperparameter panels are rearranged. Figures 9–13 move after the appendix text, retaining their imagery. Figure 6's caption also corrects the layer designation.

improvement.justification: The expanded configurations, downstream component ablations, and nonlinear-output checks strengthen evidence beyond v1's single teacher–student configuration and initialization-alignment analysis. Cost reporting also improves practical assessment. These gains are limited by underspecified subset protocols and new reporting errors: Appendix C claims a cleaner-teacher segmentation improvement over FitNet although Table 10a reports 2.78 versus 3.06 mIoU. The added evidence improves the paper, but these reliability problems prevent a stronger assessment.
